instance_recommendations.rationale: Current baseline instance. Compute-optimized with known-good performance for this workload. No migration risk.

Recommended for performance strategy. 4th-gen Intel Sapphire Rapids offers ~15% better single-thread and throughput performance over c5. The 5% cost increase is offset by faster task processing, reducing queue dwell time and potentially requiring fewer peak instances.

Highest single-core performance option available. 5th-gen Intel offers ~25% improvement over c5 generation. Best choice if minimizing queue latency is the top priority and the workload is CPU-bound. The 10% premium per instance may be partially recovered by needing fewer instances at peak.
Same price as c5.xlarge but newer Ice Lake architecture with ~10% better throughput. A no-cost upgrade path that improves processing speed without any budget impact.

rationale.scaling_policy: The policy is designed for aggressive scale-up with more granular steps to minimize queue latency, per the performance optimization strategy. Key design choices: (1) Scale-down starts only when queue depth is near zero (0-10 messages), with a moderate -3 adjustment to quickly shed idle capacity given 83% zero-depth time. A second scale-down band (10-50) with -1 provides cautious reduction to maintain headroom. (2) Scale-up triggers early at just 50 messages (down from the current 100) to build capacity before backlogs grow. (3) The upper steps are significantly more aggressive than the current policy — at 1200+ messages the adjustment is +12 and at 5000+ it is +15, reflecting the data showing extreme spikes up to ~146K messages. The p99 of ~109K and peak desired capacity of 50 confirm the workload has sharp bursts requiring rapid scaling. (4) The 300s cooldown respects the instance_drain_seconds constraint (max of 120s warmup, 300s drain) and ensures instances are fully drained before further scale-down, and fully warmed before further scale-up decisions.
rationale.strategy_impact: Performance optimization drove three main decisions: (a) lower scale-up thresholds (50 messages vs. previous 100) to reduce time-to-react, (b) higher scaling adjustments at every tier to overshoot capacity and burn through queue backlogs faster, and (c) instance type recommendations favor newer-generation compute-optimized instances (c7i, c8i, c6i) that deliver better per-core throughput even at higher cost. The max_size of 50 was observed to be fully utilized, so no reduction is recommended — if anything, the aggressive adjustments may benefit from a higher max_size in the future.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The 300s cooldown is required by the drain constraint but may delay reaction to rapid successive bursts; monitor for cases where queue grows during cooldown windows. 2) The aggressive +15 adjustment at 5000+ messages could push near the max_size=50 limit quickly — consider increasing max_size to 60-70 if peak spikes remain at ~146K. 3) Queue is at zero 83% of the time but does NOT meet the >80% sustained zero threshold for scaling to zero, and min_size=1 is retained. 4) Switching to c7i/c8i requires validating AMI compatibility and application dependencies on the newer instance families. 5) Two duplicate policies exist (scale-on-celery-meeting-briefs-py39-queue and scale-on-meeting_briefs) with identical configurations — this may cause conflicting scaling actions; consolidate to a single policy.
